parts.title: SPIRAL REVIEW (5 min)
content: 1. GRAMMAR SPIRAL: Use connectives to join these pairs of sentences: a) Dolphins are smart. They use tools. b) Tigers are endangered. Wolves are also endangered. c) Climate change is serious. Governments disagree on solutions.

2. VOCABULARY: Which graphic organizer would you use for each task? [a] compare two animals [b] show steps in photosynthesis [c] organize research on a single topic → [Venn diagram / Flow chart / Mind map]

3. MATH SPIRAL: You have 24 research notes. You group them: 6 notes on causes, 8 notes on effects, 5 notes on solutions, 5 notes on background. What percentage of notes are about effects? [8/24 × 100 = ___]

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  After gathering research notes, the next step is ORGANIZING your information. Raw notes are like puzzle pieces — you need to sort them before you can see the full picture.
content: 📖 After gathering research notes, the next step is ORGANIZING your information. Raw notes are like puzzle pieces — you need to sort them before you can see the full picture.

Graphic organizers are visual tools that help you organize information. A MIND MAP puts your main topic in the centre with branches for each sub-question. It helps you see connections between ideas. A VENN DIAGRAM uses two overlapping circles to compare two things. The overlapping section shows similarities, the outer sections show differences. A FLOW CHART shows steps in a sequence, which is useful for explaining processes.
When organizing research, you should also look for PATTERNS. Do multiple sources say the same thing? That is strong evidence. Do sources disagree? That is also interesting to write about!
The goal of organizing your notes is to create an OUTLINE — a plan for your report that lists what goes in each paragraph.
